title: Zero Dollars: 10 Things Locals Do for Free
description: Ten Moscow resets that need no ticket: sculpture walks, palace-park loops, workout stops, riverside miles, and one free shuttle.

cards.title: Ride the free VDNH shuttle
cards.subtitle: A no-fare circuit through the exhibition grounds
cards.notes: Board the electric bus beside the Main Entrance arch. VDNH states that the grounds have free admission and the shuttle is free; museums and other ticketed attractions remain separate.
cards.short_summary: Circle VDNH without paying a fare, hopping off near fountains, pavilions, Ostankino Park, or the Botanical Garden.

cards.title: Walk Tsaritsyno Park for free
cards.subtitle: Palace façades, ponds, and long landscaped paths
cards.notes: The museum’s official FAQ explicitly says admission to Tsaritsyno Park is free. Indoor exhibitions and palace rooms require separate tickets.
cards.short_summary: Use the free park as the main event: trace the ponds and bridges, then view the palace ensemble from outside.

cards.title: Browse Muzeon’s sculptures for free
cards.subtitle: An open-air art walk beside Krymsky Val
cards.notes: Moscow’s official park portal lists free admission and explains that the entry charge was removed so visitors could see the contemporary-art objects. Ticketed events may still cost extra.
cards.short_summary: Thread through the outdoor sculpture collection, then continue toward the river without crossing a ticket barrier.

cards.title: Use Izmailovsky’s courts for free
cards.subtitle: Bring a ball or paddles to the east-side park
cards.notes: The official city park page lists free admission alongside volleyball and basketball courts and six summer table-tennis tables. Bring your own equipment to avoid relying on paid rental services.
cards.short_summary: Turn a free park visit into a pickup-game afternoon on the listed courts and seasonal tennis tables.
cards.source_title: Места — Парк культуры и отдыха «Измайловский» — Мосгорпарк

cards.title: Play table tennis in Bauman Garden for free
cards.subtitle: A compact garden session near the old center
cards.notes: Moscow’s park portal confirms free garden admission and several table-tennis tables. Bring paddles and a ball; rentals and other commercial services are not included in the free claim.
cards.short_summary: Drop into the garden with your own kit for a few games among the paths and historic buildings.

cards.title: Lounge in Hermitage Garden for free
cards.subtitle: Deck chairs, table-tennis tables, and Wi-Fi off Karetny Ryad
cards.notes: The official city park page explicitly lists free admission, loungers, table-tennis tables, and park-wide Wi-Fi. Equipment rental and theater performances may carry separate charges.
cards.short_summary: Claim a lounger or bring your own table-tennis gear for a low-key pause in this central garden.

cards.title: Train on Sokolniki’s workout grounds for free
cards.subtitle: Open exercise platforms inside a round-the-clock park
cards.notes: Moscow’s official park directory states that entry is free and identifies outdoor workout platforms. Pools, rentals, attractions, and organized sports facilities may charge separately.
cards.short_summary: Build a body-weight circuit around the park’s workout platforms, with no admission ticket required.
cards.source_title: Места — Парк культуры и отдыха «Сокольники» — Мосгорпарк

cards.title: Roll through Gorky Park for free
cards.subtitle: Long paths between Krymsky Val and Neskuchny Garden
cards.notes: The city park portal explicitly lists round-the-clock free admission and says the park is suited to roller skating. Bring your own skates because rental points are commercial services.
cards.short_summary: Use the broad park paths for a no-ticket skate, extending south when you want a longer run.
cards.source_title: Еда — Центральный парк культуры и отдыха имени М. Горького — Мосгорпарк

cards.title: Roam Kolomenskoye’s grounds for free
cards.subtitle: An all-day estate walk above the Moskva River
cards.notes: Moscow’s official park directory lists Kolomenskoye as open around the clock with free admission. Museum interiors and guided programs are outside that claim.
cards.short_summary: Make a free circuit through the estate landscape and inspect its historic architecture from the public grounds.

cards.title: Follow the riverside park for free
cards.subtitle: A long public greenway in Maryino
cards.notes: Moscow’s official park directory lists Park 850-Letiya Moskvy as open around the clock with free admission. Paid rentals or concessions are optional and not part of the activity.
cards.short_summary: Take an unhurried walk through this southeastern park without an entrance fee or required purchase.
